title: Literature Review: Double Pendulum Dynamics and Simulation Methods

lagrangian_hamiltonian_derivation.title: Double pendulum (Wikipedia)
lagrangian_hamiltonian_derivation.key_findings: Complete derivation of equations of motion using Lagrangian mechanics. Defines generalized coordinates (theta1, theta2), kinetic/potential energy, Euler-Lagrange equations. Standard reference for the coupled nonlinear ODEs.

lagrangian_hamiltonian_derivation.title: Double pendulum: Lagrangian formulation (dassencio.org)
lagrangian_hamiltonian_derivation.key_findings: Clear derivation with explicit expressions for angular accelerations. Companion Hamiltonian formulation also available. Used as basis for the dassencio/double-pendulum Python simulator.

lagrangian_hamiltonian_derivation.title: The Double Pendulum (SciPython)
lagrangian_hamiltonian_derivation.key_findings: Python implementation with matplotlib animation. Uses scipy.integrate.odeint for numerical integration. Good pedagogical resource showing the complete workflow from equations to visualization.

numerical_integration_methods.title: Hairer, Lubich, Wanner - Geometric Numerical Integration (2006)
numerical_integration_methods.key_findings: Definitive reference on structure-preserving numerical methods. Covers symplectic integrators (Stormer-Verlet, leapfrog, higher-order splitting methods), backward error analysis, and long-term energy behavior. Shows that symplectic integrators preserve a modified Hamiltonian, leading to bounded energy oscillations.

numerical_integration_methods.title: Symplectic integrator (Wikipedia)
numerical_integration_methods.key_findings: Comprehensive overview of symplectic integration methods. Stormer-Verlet is 2nd-order, time-reversible, area-preserving. For separable Hamiltonians H=T+V, the method becomes explicit. Higher-order methods via Yoshida composition.

numerical_integration_methods.title: Deterministic chaos: A pedagogical review of the double pendulum case (SciELO, 2024)
numerical_integration_methods.key_findings: Comprehensive pedagogical review using 4th-order Runge-Kutta. Covers Hamiltonian formalism, Python implementation, Lyapunov exponent computation. Discusses computational efficiency considerations.

chaos_lyapunov_exponents.title: Shinbrot, Grebogi, Wisdom, Yorke - Chaos in a double pendulum (1992)
chaos_lyapunov_exponents.key_findings: Foundational paper. Experimental Lyapunov exponent: 7.5 +/- 1.5 s^-1. Numerical: 7.9 +/- 0.4 s^-1. Demonstrates sensitive dependence on initial conditions both experimentally and numerically. Published in American Journal of Physics 60, 491-499.

chaos_lyapunov_exponents.title: Stachowiak & Okada - A numerical analysis of chaos in the double pendulum (2006)
chaos_lyapunov_exponents.key_findings: Poincare sections and bifurcation diagrams at different energy levels. Uses Bulirsch-Stoer method with Richardson extrapolation. Shows transition from regular to chaotic motion as energy increases. Lyapunov exponents confirm: zero at low energy, positive at high energy.

chaos_lyapunov_exponents.title: Jimenez Lopez & Garcia Garrido - Chaos and Regularity in the Double Pendulum with Lagrangian Descriptors (2024)
chaos_lyapunov_exponents.key_findings: Uses Lagrangian descriptors to characterize chaotic vs regular regions. Key finding: maximum chaotic fraction occurs at equal pendulum lengths for a given mass ratio. Parametric study of chaos growth/decay vs energy and model parameters. Published in IJBC 34(16), 2450201.

poincare_sections_bifurcation.title: Stachowiak & Okada 2006 (same as above)
poincare_sections_bifurcation.key_findings: Poincare sections constructed with surface u1=0, du1/dt>0. Shows regular motion at low energy, mixed phase space at moderate energy, and global chaos at high energy.

poincare_sections_bifurcation.title: Poincare section clicker (Leo C. Stein)
poincare_sections_bifurcation.key_findings: Interactive tool for exploring Poincare sections. Demonstrates: quasiperiodic orbits trace curves, chaotic orbits fill areas. Low energy shows nested tori (integrable-like), high energy shows dust (chaos).

poincare_sections_bifurcation.title: Regular and chaotic phase space fraction in the double pendulum (arXiv 2023)
poincare_sections_bifurcation.key_findings: Studies transition between regular and chaotic behavior globally. Computes fraction of initial conditions leading to chaos via Poincare sections. Chaotic fraction near zero at low energy (small oscillations approximation valid).

flip_count_maps_fractals.title: Heyl - The Double Pendulum Fractal
flip_count_maps_fractals.key_findings: Flip-time maps with theta1, theta2 in [-pi, pi]. Color indicates elapsed time before first flip. Shows fractal boundary structure. Energetic constraint: 3cos(theta1)+cos(theta2)>2 prevents flipping.

flip_count_maps_fractals.title: A novel global perspective: fractal basins in double pendulum (2024)
flip_count_maps_fractals.key_findings: Proposes algorithms for computing flip count and final angular position. Reveals petal-like structure with rotational symmetry and fractal features. Uses average maximum Lyapunov exponent heatmap to correlate mass ratio with chaos level.
